quantities.V1: record boundary distance from the deed call to be retraced (feet)
quantities.V2: traverse misclosure ratio (measured-vs-record discrepancy as a fraction)
quantities.V3: found-monument offset from the computed corner position (hundredths of a foot, scaled)
quantities.V4: control network parameter (length of tied control traverse to recovered monuments, feet)
quantities.ANNEX_SEVERITY: severity of the title or monument-conflict exception noted in the annex (0 = clean, 1 = irreconcilable)

tier3_rule: adjusted_line * (1 - REG.proration_rate * eff_sev) - REG.encroachment_setback * REG.acquiescence_mult * V3
draft.rationale: A boundary survey retraces a deed call (V1) and weights it by how well it ties into the control network (V4). The resolved line is then corrected for the found-monument offset (V3) and the traverse misclosure (V2). The public rules mirror handbook practice: plain record retracement when nothing is wrong, a closure-tolerance adjustment when misclosure is present, and an explicit monument-conflict reduction scaled by the annex exception severity. The unwritten convention is how field surveyors prorate a discrepancy under senior-rights doctrine. When misclosure reaches about 1 in 7 (V2 >= 0.14, which is not a published tolerance), they discount the record line more heavily by the conflict severity. They still credit strong control ties and penalize monument offsets. The precedent rule reflects case law on acquiescence and adverse possession: past rulings fix an amplification of severity by misclosure, a proration rate and an encroachment setback factor, held as private registry constants. Calculation and verification (the Middle and Outer ring tasks) sit in V2 and V3. The legally anchored boundary determination (the Inner task) drives which rule applies.
